day.reading: standing variation shortens only the wait; recombination cannot close the gap; the LTEE is a worst case for supply only, and s and Ne are worse in humans
day.holds: the cut from standing variation is bounded by a factor of two (p0 <= 0.5), small against the shortfalls; the LTEE does under-supply mutations (kappa 93,659, a concession Day makes at L16); interference under linkage is real (A2e, R4 F2 credit)

critic.reading: a clonal, nonrecombining, zero-polymorphism start makes the LTEE rate inapt for humans
critic.holds: 'cannot reduce the fixation time once selection begins' is false as stated: 26.8% at p0 = 0.01, 35.1% at 0.05; the LTEE ceiling holds only under a stated transfer factor (M-006), and the recombining asymptote (17.5-19 per generation, W&B) is set by map length, not by the clonal rate, though the clonal LTEE is outside W&B's domain

notes: Model-choice: no single number settles transfer. New arithmetic: the standing-variation cut, exact under M-601's deterministic sweep (s cancels in the ratio; stochastic establishment and the prior neutral phase are not modelled). The other numbers are cited from M-006 and claim file A2e. Day's 'roughly 30,000 times slower in real time' (evo005@L16) and the Lynch relay are not checked: the population sizes behind the first are not stated and the Lynch book is not held. Whether critics hold that humans fixate faster than bacteria per generation (evo005@L2) is a fidelity question for the claim files.
